_schema_notes: Grad-scholarship-specific dataset, separate from backend/data/programs.json. Each entry: id, name, scope ('global'|'nigeria'), provider, degree_levels[], study_destination, fields_of_study, nationality_eligibility, financial_need_required, min_academic_requirement, work_experience_required, benefit, eligibility[], required_documents[], essay_or_interview {required, essay_topics[], interview}, application_process, apply_url, deadline_note, status, confidence, source_url, source_checked, notes. essay_topics are REAL, previously-used prompt themes where known — the AI Essay Predictor may only draw from these plus the user's own profile; it must never invent a topic for a scholarship with an empty essay_topics list.

scholarships.name: Chevening Scholarship
scholarships.study_destination: United Kingdom (any UK university, applicant's choice)
scholarships.nationality_eligibility: Citizens of eligible Chevening countries, including Nigeria
scholarships.min_academic_requirement: Undergraduate degree that qualifies for UK master's admission, completed at least 2 years before the deadline
scholarships.work_experience_required: At least 2,800 hours (roughly 2 years) of work experience — full-time, part-time, or voluntary
scholarships.benefit: Fully funded one-year UK master's degree: tuition, monthly stipend, return flights, and additional grants/allowances
eligibility: Citizen of an eligible Chevening country (Nigeria is eligible)
Return home for at least 2 years after the award ends
At least 2,800 hours of work experience
Undergraduate degree completed 2+ years before the application deadline
Apply to and receive admission offers from at least 3 eligible UK university courses
No UK-government-funded scholarship in the past 12 months
required_documents: Four required essays (leadership, networking, course choice, career plan — 300 words each)

essay_topics: Networking experience and how you'll use Chevening's alumni network
Why this course, and why now
Career plan — including your commitment to return home after the scholarship

scholarships.application_process: Apply online via Chevening's own portal; separately secure admission to at least 3 eligible UK university courses
scholarships.deadline_note: 2027/2028 cycle: opened 4 Aug 2026, closes 6 Oct 2026, 11:00 UTC — recheck for next cycle
scholarships.status: cycle-dependent — recheck chevening.org before presenting a live deadline
scholarships.source_url: aggregator sources (cheveningprep.com, scholarshipregion.com, everythingabuad.com) converge on eligibility/essays/deadline; chevening.org is Chevening's own official domain
scholarships.notes: Strong, consistent detail across sources including the exact essay structure — one of the better-sourced entries in this dataset. Deadline is annual and moves each cycle; always confirm the current window on chevening.org.

scholarships.name: Fulbright Foreign Student Program (Nigeria — PhD track)
scholarships.provider: U.S. Department of State / U.S. Embassy Nigeria
scholarships.min_academic_requirement: Outstanding academic record; must already be at least 2 years into a doctoral program
scholarships.work_experience_required: Endorsement of home institution as an academic-staff-track doctoral candidate
scholarships.benefit: Funded research/study period in the United States to advance an in-progress PhD, plus academic and cultural exchange support
eligibility: Nigerian citizen
At least 2 years into a doctoral (PhD) program at a Nigerian university or research institute
Endorsement from home institution
Outstanding academic record and strong English proficiency
Minimum TOEFL score of 90 (or equivalent)
scholarships.application_process: Apply online via the Fulbright Foreign Student Program application, coordinated through the U.S. Embassy in Nigeria
scholarships.deadline_note: Strict deadline historically around 1 June — recheck for the current cycle
scholarships.status: needs_verification — exact current-cycle deadline not independently confirmed
scholarships.source_url: us.fulbrightonline.org (Nigeria country pages) and ng.usembassy.gov (U.S. Embassy Nigeria's own domain), plus scholarshipportal.ng aggregator coverage
scholarships.notes: IMPORTANT: for Nigeria specifically, this Fulbright track is PhD-only — applicants must already be 2+ years into a doctoral programme at a Nigerian institution. Masters applicants and first-degree holders are explicitly NOT eligible under this Nigeria-specific track (other Fulbright tracks exist globally with different rules — don't generalize this restriction to other countries).
scholarships.essay_topics_caveat: No specific essay prompts found publicly — do not invent any; note in the UI that essay topics are set case-by-case.

scholarships.name: DAAD EPOS Scholarship (Development-Related Postgraduate Courses)
scholarships.fields_of_study: any, via a specific list of EPOS-affiliated postgraduate courses
scholarships.nationality_eligibility: Graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries, including Nigeria
scholarships.min_academic_requirement: Bachelor's degree (typically 4-year), completed no more than 6 years before application
scholarships.work_experience_required: Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience
scholarships.benefit: Full funding for a Master's (up to 2 years) or PhD (up to 3.5 years) at a German university: monthly stipend (~€992 Master's / ~€1,300-1,400 PhD), health/accident/liability insurance, and other allowances
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in an appropriate subject
Degree completed within the last 6 years
At least 2 years of relevant professional experience
From a DAAD-eligible developing/newly industrialised country (Nigeria qualifies)
required_documents: Language proficiency evidence (German or English, depending on course)

essay_topics: Motivation letter tailored to the chosen EPOS course and its development relevance

scholarships.application_process: Applications are submitted directly to the chosen EPOS-affiliated course (not to DAAD centrally) — select up to 3 postgraduate programmes from the EPOS list and apply via each course's own procedure
scholarships.deadline_note: Roughly one year ahead of intended admission — e.g. 15 October 2026 for a course starting October 2027; varies by course
scholarships.status: ongoing — deadlines vary per affiliated course, recheck the specific programme
scholarships.source_url: daad.de and www2.daad.de (DAAD's own domains) plus aggregator coverage (mastersportal.com, opportunitiesforafricans.com) for stipend figures and deadline pattern
scholarships.notes: Unlike most scholarships here, EPOS has no single central application — the real deadline and process depend entirely on which of the many EPOS-listed courses the applicant picks. Treat the deadline_note as a general pattern, not a fixed date.

scholarships.name: Commonwealth Scholarships (Masters & PhD)
scholarships.fields_of_study: any, with some development-relevant priority themes
scholarships.nationality_eligibility: Citizens of developing Commonwealth countries, including Nigeria
scholarships.min_academic_requirement: Masters: first degree with at least Second Class Upper. PhD: Second Class Lower accepted, plus a relevant master's degree
scholarships.benefit: Fully funded UK Master's or PhD: tuition, living stipend, airfare, and other allowances
eligibility: Citizen of a developing Commonwealth country (Nigeria qualifies)
Masters: minimum Second Class Upper first degree
PhD: minimum Second Class Lower first degree plus a relevant master's degree
Admission offers from at least 2 UK institutions
NYSC discharge or exemption certificate (Nigerian applicants)
Unable to fund UK study independently — financial need is a stated eligibility criterion, not just a preference
scholarships.application_process: Apply online via the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission's own portal (separate Masters and PhD tracks); Nigerian applicants may also need endorsement routed through the Federal Ministry of Education
scholarships.deadline_note: 2027/2028 cycle: on or before 20 October 2026 — recheck for the current cycle
scholarships.status: cycle-dependent — recheck cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk before presenting a live deadline
scholarships.source_url: cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk (the Commission's own domain) plus education.gov.ng (Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Education advert PDF) and aggregator coverage (scholars4dev.com, arbiterz.com)
scholarships.notes: Financial need is an explicit, stated eligibility criterion here (unlike Chevening) — flag this clearly to users who can self-fund, since they likely won't qualify regardless of academic strength. PhD track name in the source is specifically for 'least developed countries and vulnerable states' — Nigeria's exact PhD-track eligibility should be reconfirmed on cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk.

scholarships.name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
scholarships.provider: Mastercard Foundation, via 60+ partner universities worldwide
scholarships.study_destination: Varies by partner university (e.g. Cambridge, Edinburgh, Toronto, and African partner institutions)
scholarships.fields_of_study: any full-time master's programme offered by a partner university
scholarships.nationality_eligibility: From and living in an African country (temporary study/work abroad is fine)
scholarships.min_academic_requirement: Strong academic achievement (varies by partner institution's own admission bar)
scholarships.benefit: Full funding: tuition, accommodation, books, transportation, and a living stipend, tied to whichever partner university admits the applicant
eligibility: From and living in an African country (Nigeria qualifies)
28 years old or younger at application (32 or younger for Refugee/Persons-with-Disabilities categories)
Demonstrated financial hardship
Strong academic achievement and leadership potential
Commitment to giving back to community/home country/Africa, and to sustainability/climate resilience themes
required_documents: needs_verification — varies by partner institution, but typically CV, transcripts, references, and a personal statement

essay_topics: Commitment to giving back to your community, home country, or Africa

scholarships.application_process: Apply directly to a Mastercard Foundation Scholars partner university's own master's admissions process, then opt into the Scholars Program during that application
scholarships.deadline_note: Varies by partner university; one commonly cited deadline is 15 November 2026
scholarships.status: ongoing — exact deadline depends entirely on which partner university/programme is chosen
scholarships.source_url: mastercardfdn.org (the Foundation's own domain) plus partner-university pages (mastercardfoundation.fund.cam.ac.uk) and aggregator coverage
scholarships.notes: This is not a single centralized scholarship — each of 60+ partner universities runs its own admissions and Scholars selection, with different deadlines and specific requirements. Treat this entry as a starting point, not a single application.

scholarships.name: Australia Awards Scholarships (Africa — Master's)
scholarships.fields_of_study: Priority areas for Nigeria typically include public health, agricultural science/food security, infrastructure, public policy/governance, and education
scholarships.nationality_eligibility: Citizens of participating African countries, including Nigeria
scholarships.min_academic_requirement: needs_verification — general Australia Awards academic-merit bar, not separately confirmed for the Africa programme
scholarships.benefit: Fully funded Australian Master's degree: tuition, living stipend, travel, and health cover
eligibility: Citizen of a participating African country (Nigeria qualifies)
Applying for a Master's degree only — the Africa programme does not offer PhD scholarships
First apply for admission to an eligible Master's programme at an Australian university
required_documents: needs_verification — typically degree transcripts, references, English proficiency test (IELTS/TOEFL), and admission evidence
scholarships.application_process: Apply online via the OASIS portal, managed through the Australian High Commission in Abuja for Nigerian applicants
scholarships.deadline_note: Recently cited deadline: 30 April 2026, 14:00 AEST — recheck for the current cycle
scholarships.status: cycle-dependent — recheck before presenting a live deadline
scholarships.source_url: dfat.gov.au (Australian Government's own domain) plus aggregator coverage (australiaawardshub.com, migrationvisportal.com)
scholarships.notes: IMPORTANT: PhD is NOT available under the Africa-specific Australia Awards programme — Master's only. Don't match PhD-seeking users to this entry.

scholarships.name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's Degrees
scholarships.study_destination: Multiple European universities (a consortium — study across 2+ countries per programme)
scholarships.fields_of_study: varies by joint programme — hundreds of EMJMD programmes exist across disciplines
scholarships.min_academic_requirement: Bachelor's degree, plus programme-specific admission requirements
scholarships.benefit: Full tuition, ~€1,400/month stipend for up to 24 months (~€33,600 total), health insurance, and travel/installation allowances
eligibility: Bachelor's degree
Meets the specific joint programme's own admission criteria
Not a national of the country where the coordinating institution is based, for certain scholarship categories (varies by programme)
required_documents: needs_verification — varies by programme, but typically transcripts, CV, motivation letter, references, language proficiency

essay_topics: Motivation letter specific to the chosen joint programme

scholarships.application_process: Browse the official EMJMD catalogue, then apply directly to the chosen joint programme/consortium — no single central Erasmus Mundus application
scholarships.deadline_note: Varies by programme — most fall between October and January for the following academic year's intake
scholarships.status: ongoing — deadlines are set per individual joint programme, not centrally
scholarships.source_url: erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu (European Commission's own domain) plus aggregator coverage (mastersportal.com, globalsouthacademia.com)
scholarships.notes: Like DAAD EPOS, this is an umbrella — the real deadline, essay expectations, and requirements depend entirely on which of the many EMJMD programmes the applicant picks from the official catalogue.

scholarships.name: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
scholarships.provider: Gates Cambridge Trust, University of Cambridge
scholarships.fields_of_study: any full-time PhD, MLitt, or eligible one-year postgraduate course
scholarships.nationality_eligibility: Open globally, including Nigeria (any country outside the UK)
scholarships.min_academic_requirement: Outstanding academic record — average Gates Scholar GPA is around 3.92/4.0
scholarships.benefit: Full funding at Cambridge: university and college fees, maintenance allowance, and additional allowances
eligibility: Citizen of a country outside the UK (Nigeria qualifies)
Applying for full-time or part-time PhD, full-time MLitt, or an eligible one-year postgraduate course at Cambridge
Outstanding academic record
Demonstrated intellectual distinction (honors, awards, prior recognition)
Strong preparation for the proposed field of graduate study
required_documents: Cambridge course/college application (the Gates Cambridge application is embedded within it)
scholarships.application_process: Apply for admission to a Cambridge course and college first, then complete the Gates Cambridge funding section within the same application
scholarships.deadline_note: 2026 cycle: 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, depending on the specific course — recheck the course's own deadline
scholarships.status: cycle-dependent — recheck gatescambridge.org and the specific Cambridge course deadline
scholarships.source_url: aggregator sources (scholars4dev.com, globalsouthacademia.com, crispng.com) converge on eligibility/deadlines; gatescambridge.org is the Trust's own official domain
scholarships.notes: Extremely competitive — the average admitted GPA (3.92/4.0) is worth surfacing explicitly in gap analysis so users can calibrate expectations realistically rather than assume typical postgrad grades are competitive here.

scholarships.benefit: Fully funded overseas Master's/PhD: tuition, return airfare, accommodation/living allowance, health insurance
eligibility: Nigerian citizen
Admission or enrollment eligibility in an eligible priority field (engineering, geosciences, energy studies, environmental sciences, technology development)
needs_verification for exact academic threshold — likely a strong first-degree or master's result
required_documents: needs_verification — likely admission letter, transcripts, means of ID; overseas track likely requires an offer from a partner university

scholarships.deadline_note: 2026 cycle applications closed 5 June 2026; reopens annually — recheck before demo
scholarships.status: 2026 cycle closed; reopens annually — recheck scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng
scholarships.source_url: Same sourcing as the ptdf_scholarship entry in programs.json — scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng (fetched directly, confirmed real portal) plus aggregator corroboration

scholarships.name: TETFund Academic Staff Training and Development (AST&D)
scholarships.study_destination: Nigeria only (in-country) — foreign/overseas sponsorship under this fund is currently suspended
scholarships.nationality_eligibility: Nigerian academic staff of eligible tertiary institutions
scholarships.min_academic_requirement: Full-time, confirmed academic staff status at an eligible Nigerian tertiary institution, with secured admission to a National Universities Commission (NUC)-approved graduate programme
scholarships.work_experience_required: Must be a confirmed (not probationary) academic staff member
scholarships.benefit: Funded Master's or PhD study at a Nigerian university, for confirmed academic staff
eligibility: Full-time, confirmed academic staff at an eligible Nigerian tertiary institution
Secured admission to an NUC-approved graduate programme within Nigeria
Not already registered for the programme independently before applying (must apply before registering)
Not seeking a second Master's or second PhD
scholarships.application_process: Apply through your institution's Academic Planning Unit, addressed to the Vice-Chancellor/Rector, with the required nomination documents — no central online portal
scholarships.deadline_note: needs_verification — each institution runs its own submission window/cycle
scholarships.status: ongoing, in-country only — overseas AST&D sponsorship currently suspended
scholarships.source_url: university-published notices (unilag.edu.ng, unn.edu.ng, ui.edu.ng) describing TETFund's own AST&D guidelines; tetfund.gov.ng is the Fund's own domain
scholarships.notes: IMPORTANT: this scholarship is restricted to confirmed academic staff already employed by a Nigerian tertiary institution — it is NOT open to the general public or to students without an academic-staff appointment. Only match this to users who describe being lecturers/academic staff pursuing further study. Also flag clearly that overseas sponsorship under this fund is currently suspended — in-country only.
